Cross-checked over the importer population the manifest names: logs/importer-base.log and logs/importer-after.log each carry 18 FAILED/ERROR ids and comm over the two sorted id sets returns none added and none fixed.

1.reason: the guard for that case is attempts == [1], which reddens if another checkout's lock is waited on; the self-constructed path comparison is a fixture sanity check, not the coverage claim

findings.summary: the loop condition is "while retries + 1 < attempts and _failed_on_this_index_lock(lock, result)", and that predicate never reads result.returncode
findings.text: blocking: the loop condition is "while retries + 1 < attempts and _failed_on_this_index_lock(lock, result)", and that predicate never reads result.returncode, so a successful step is retried whenever this checkout's index.lock exists at the check, either because a peer created it between the call returning and the check or through the lock.exists() fallback at merge.py:822; the old condition required returncode != 0 and the docstring at merge.py:838 still says the step runs until it succeeds. land_merge's step at merge.py:1174 runs git merge --ff-only and its retry re-reads base from the moved HEAD at merge.py:1155, so a retried success lands a second merge commit on the primary branch; promotion_scope.py:2940's git commit --only re-run after a successful commit returns "nothing to commit", driving the caller at promotion_scope.py:2958 into rollback and reporting a landed commit as failed, and reckon/ledger.py:3113's commit step reaches the same false failure. Repair by keeping the guard, "result.returncode != 0 and _failed_on_this_index_lock(lock, result)", and add a case asserting a successful call with the lock present returns after one attempt.

findings.summary: assert str(other_lock) != str(_lock(repo)) compares two paths the test itself constructed and never calls the code under test
findings.text: non-blocking: assert str(other_lock) != str(_lock(repo)) compares two paths the test itself constructed and never calls the code under test, so it holds whatever the helper does and reads as coverage it does not provide; the guard in that case is attempts == [1] at line 229, which does redden if another checkout's lock is waited on.

findings.summary: the holder subprocess is given 50 ms to notice the release file and unlink the lock, and line 134 asserts released_after[0] < 0.05
findings.text: non-blocking: the holder subprocess is given 50 ms to notice the release file and unlink the lock, and line 134 asserts released_after[0] < 0.05, so on a loaded shared node the case can fail for scheduler latency rather than for anything the helper did; the property the case needs is only that the lock is gone before the retry reads it.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 251cb1cd: bcc56fcc adds _result_text and _failed_on_this_index_lock and rewrites the retry condition plus two docstrings in reckon/crew/merge.py; efeb0d0d4339 adds only the 37-line evidence fragment; three files, 306 insertions and 7 deletions.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_a_landing_commit_retries_a_released_lock.py passing every plan case, the base revision failing the released-lock case, and no added importer failure; after-arm.log at efeb0d0d4339 records 59 passed EXIT=0, base-arm.log at 251cb1cd records 55 passed EXIT=0, negative-control.log records 1 failed and 3 passed EXIT=1 naming test_a_lock_released_after_the_failed_call_still_waits, and the importer arms carry 18 identical failure ids either side, all four logs reopened by this review.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to retry a git call refused by this checkout's index lock even when the lock is gone by the time the wait helper looks, up to the same bound; reckon/crew/merge.py:807-822 adds _failed_on_this_index_lock, which reads the failure's own text for this checkout's lock path before falling back to the file, and merge.py:867 applies it inside the existing bounded loop, so the goal is met.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it reports status complete, two commits at bcc56fcc and efeb0d0d4339, a focused gate of 59 passed against a 55-passed base arm, a negative control failing only the released-lock case, a clean worktree, and 18 pre-existing importer failures at both arms.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared paths are reckon/crew/merge.py, tests/test_a_landing_commit_retries_a_released_lock.py, a fragment under docs/evidence/fragments/a-landing-never-waits-on-a-shared-index/ and a figures directory; the diff touches the first three and nothing outside them.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_landing_commit_retries_a_released_lock.py:128 asserts attempts == [1, 2] and negative-control.log shows that assertion reddening at the base revision, but no test asserts that a successful call with the lock present returns after one attempt, so the regression merge.py:867 introduces is unguarded.
justifications.evidence: the three arms are recorded in logs I reopened and their summary lines and EXIT codes match the manifest, though the importer head arm ran at bcc56fcc rather than efeb0d0d4339 and that second commit is docs-only.
justifications.fit: merge.py:807-809 names and documents the new predicate for a failed call while merge.py:867 applies it to every result including successful ones, where the surrounding helpers at merge.py:706-720 keep name and contract aligned.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/merge.py:820-822 returns the failure's own naming of this checkout's lock before falling back to lock.exists(), which is exactly the released-lock case the goal names.
justifications.reuse: the change extends _run_waiting_out_a_held_index_lock at merge.py:825 rather than forking it and reuses _index_lock_held and the caller's bound, and _result_text at merge.py:796 has no owner in the repository, the nearest idiom being the inline stderr.strip() or stdout.strip() at merge.py:296 and reckon/ledger.py:3183.
justifications.scope_discipline: the three changed files sit inside the four declared paths, but merge.py:867 also drops the loop's result.returncode != 0 guard, which is a behavioural change the goal does not imply.
